sharedLearningVideo.title: Equivalent fractions
sharedLearningVideo.description: See how different fractions can represent the same part of a whole.

blocks.name: Reading Comprehension
blocks.description: Understand a passage, find the main idea and answer questions using details from the text.

questions.passage: Mira waters a seed each morning. She moves the pot into the sunshine and watches a tiny shoot appear.
questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Mira helps a seed grow
How to paint a flower pot
questions.explanation: Each detail describes one way Mira cares for her seed or what happens as it grows.

questions.passage: Mira waters a seed each morning. She moves the pot into the sunshine and watches a tiny shoot appear.
questions.prompt: Which detail shows that Mira is taking care of the seed?
options: She leaves the pot in a cupboard
questions.explanation: Watering the seed each morning is one of the ways Mira helps it grow.

resources.title: Key ideas and details
resources.description: Listen to a short explanation with an example.
resources.transcript: What is the main idea? It is what a passage is mostly about. Mira waters a seed and moves it into the sunlight. One morning a tiny shoot appears. These details support the main idea: Mira helps a seed grow. After reading, ask yourself: what do most of the details tell me?

resources.title: A seed for Mira
resources.description:
Mira planted a seed in a little pot. Each morning she gave it water and set it near a sunny window. One morning, a tiny green shoot pushed through the soil.

Think about it
What is the passage mainly about? Which details support your answer?

resources.title: A little seed
resources.description: A short poem about a seed waking up.
resources.transcript: A little seed lay snug below, and waited for the rain. The sunshine warmed the sleepy earth, then green slipped up again. A tiny leaf looked at the sky, a root reached down below. With drops of rain and morning light, the little seed could grow.

resources.title: Grow, little garden
resources.description: Sing along about sunlight and rain.
resources.transcript: Grow little garden, reach for the sun. Sip up the raindrops, one by one. Roots in the ground and leaves in the light. Grow little garden, green and bright.

blocks.name: Words in context
blocks.description: Use clues in the passage to work out what unfamiliar words mean.

questions.prompt: The trail was steep, so we climbed slowly. What does steep mean?
questions.explanation: The word climbed and the need to slow down suggest the path rose sharply.

questions.prompt: Ravi was relieved when he found his missing notebook. What does relieved mean?
questions.explanation: Finding the missing notebook ended the reason Ravi was worried.

blocks.name: Multiplication and Division
blocks.description: Solve everyday problems by making equal groups and sharing items equally.

questions.prompt: There are 6 baskets with 4 apples in each basket. How many apples are there?
questions.explanation: Six equal groups of four is 6 × 4, which equals 24.

questions.prompt: Share 32 pencils equally among 8 students. How many pencils does each student get?
questions.explanation: Divide 32 by 8. Each student gets 4 pencils because 8 × 4 = 32.

resources.title: Draw equal groups
resources.description:
Draw six circles. Put four dots in each circle. Count the dots, then write a multiplication sentence.

Try it again
Draw eight circles. Share 32 dots equally across them. How many dots are in each circle?

blocks.name: Plants Around Us
blocks.description: Explore how roots and sunlight help plants grow.

questions.prompt: Which part usually takes in water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water from the soil and help anchor the plant.

questions.prompt: Why should we put a growing seedling near a sunny window?
options: Light keeps roots out of soil
questions.explanation: Leaves use energy from light to make food for the plant.

resources.title: Look closely at a plant
resources.description:
Find a plant you can observe safely. Sketch its leaves and stem. Label the roots if you can see them.

What can each part do to help the plant grow?

blocks.name: Our Environment
blocks.description: Explore ways to reduce waste and care for shared spaces.

questions.prompt: What can you do to reduce waste at school?
options: Take a new plastic cup each day
Put food scraps in a paper-recycling bin
questions.explanation: Refilling a reusable bottle reduces the need for single-use cups and bottles.

questions.prompt: After a picnic in a park, what should you do with an empty snack wrapper?
options: Put it in a waste bin
questions.explanation: Putting the wrapper in a waste bin keeps the shared park clean.

resources.title: Care for your neighbourhood
resources.description:
Look around your neighbourhood with an adult. List one thing people can reuse and one place they can keep clean.

Choose a small action that you can take this week.

blocks.name: People in Our Community
blocks.description: Explore how people who work in libraries and near schools help their community.

questions.prompt: Who helps people borrow books from a public library?
questions.explanation: A librarian helps people find and borrow books at the library.

questions.prompt: Who helps people stay safe when crossing a busy road near school?
questions.explanation: A crossing guard helps people cross the road safely.

blocks.name: Story Sequence
blocks.description: Put story events in order and identify what happens before and after each event.

questions.prompt: Tara packed her bag, walked to school, and met her friend at the gate. What happened first?
questions.explanation: Packing her bag is the first event named in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which event happened right before Tara met her friend?
questions.explanation: The sentence lists walking to school immediately before meeting her friend.

resources.title: Retell a routine
resources.description: Write three steps you take before school. Use first, next, and finally to put them in order.

blocks.name: Materials and Their Uses
blocks.description: Explore how the properties of materials make them suitable for everyday uses.

questions.prompt: Which material would work best for a bag that needs to keep books dry?
questions.explanation: Water does not pass through an intact plastic sheet easily.

questions.prompt: Why is glass useful in a window?
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent, so light can travel through it.

resources.title: Test a material
resources.description: With an adult, put a drop of water on a sheet of paper and on a washable plastic lid. Compare what happens.

blocks.name: Place Value
blocks.description: Use hundreds, tens and ones to read and build three-digit numbers.

questions.prompt: What is the value of the digit 6 in 463?
questions.explanation: The 6 is in the tens place, so it represents 60.

questions.prompt: Which number has 3 hundreds, 8 tens, and 2 ones?
questions.explanation: 300 plus 80 plus 2 equals 382.

resources.title: Make a place-value table
resources.description: Label three columns Hundreds, Tens, and Ones. Place each digit of 572 in its column.

blocks.name: Maps and Symbols
blocks.description: Read map symbols and use a key to explain what they represent.

questions.prompt: A blue line is labelled “river” in a map key. What does a blue line show on the map?
questions.explanation: The key tells you the meaning of each symbol.

questions.prompt: What helps someone understand your sketch map?
questions.explanation: A key connects each symbol to the thing it represents.

resources.title: Sketch a map
resources.description: Draw a simple map of one room. Use a symbol for the door and another for a window. Add a map key.

blocks.name: Writing Clear Instructions
blocks.description: Use action words and put steps in order to write clear instructions.

questions.prompt: Which instruction begins with an action verb?
questions.explanation: Divide tells the reader what to do.

questions.prompt: Which instruction should come before pouring water into a cup?
options: Place an empty cup on the table
questions.explanation: The cup needs to be ready before you pour into it.

resources.title: Explain a task
resources.description: Write clear instructions for folding a sheet of paper in half. Start each step with a verb.

blocks.name: Understanding Fractions
blocks.description: Describe equal parts of a whole using fractions.

questions.prompt: Three of eight equal slices are left. What fraction is left?
questions.explanation: Three of eight equal slices means three eighths.

questions.prompt: Which shows one quarter?
questions.explanation: One quarter is one of four equal parts.

resources.title: Draw equal parts
resources.description: Draw a rectangle and split it into four equal parts. Shade one part, then label the fraction.

blocks.name: Weather Observations
blocks.description: Use tools and everyday observations to describe temperature and wind.

questions.prompt: What helps us measure air temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.prompt: Which observation shows that it is windy?
questions.explanation: Moving leaves show the air is moving.

resources.title: Keep a weather log
resources.description: Look outside at the same time for three days. Record temperature, clouds, and signs of wind.

blocks.name: People Who Help Us
blocks.description: Explore how libraries and public transport help people in a community.

questions.prompt: Who usually helps look after books in a public library?
questions.explanation: A librarian helps people find, borrow, and return books.

questions.prompt: Which service takes people from one stop to another?
questions.explanation: Public transport connects places by carrying passengers between stops.

resources.title: Find a community service
resources.description: Choose a place in your community that helps people. Write down who works there and what they do.
